eligibility.evidence: Main text Methods and SI prompts: open-weight LLMs given the IDAQ (Waytz et al. 2010, human baseline n=500) and three ToM benchmarks (MoToMQA, HI-ToM, SimpleToM) with and without safety ablation. Borderline because the ToM items come from AI benchmarks and the IDAQ is a trait-style questionnaire.

E.headline: Safety ablation raises mind-attribution and self-attribution but leaves ToM accuracy unchanged, so the two are dissociable; safe models under-attribute mind to animals relative to humans.

G.notes: Gemma coded family other. Ablation (not prompt change) is the manipulation; IDAQ rows coded effect with no human-typical effect, human means compared only descriptively (below human before, above after, except animals). Temperature 1 stated for mind-attribution items; ToM temperature unstated. No code link. MMLU and MoToMQA factual are controls, not coded.
